title: Nefertiti
objective: After this level you can describe Nefertiti's role and her famous portrait bust.
summary: Nefertiti, Akhenaten’s queen, appears in art with a royal role. Her bust was found at Amarna in 1912; whether she later ruled as co-regent is debated.

cards.headline: Nefertiti’s famous bust has only one inlaid eye. Nobody knows for certain why.
cards.body: That missing eye is just one of the mysteries around Akhenaten’s queen.

cards.headline: Beside the king
cards.body: Nefertiti was Akhenaten’s queen, and she was never in the background. She worshipped the Aten alongside him and was shown at the same scale as the king. Some scenes even show her smiting Egypt’s enemies, a motif previously reserved for the pharaoh. Her name is usually translated “a beautiful woman has come.”

cards.headline: The bust
cards.body: On 6 December 1912, a German team led by Ludwig Borchardt found a painted limestone bust of Nefertiti at Amarna, in the workshop of the sculptor Thutmose. It is now in the Neues Museum in Berlin. Only the right eye has an inlay, and many think the bust was a model kept in the workshop for sculptors to copy. A masterpiece that may have been a reference sheet.
cards.callout: Found in a sculptor’s workshop, not a tomb

cards.headline: Queen, co-ruler or king?
cards.body: What Nefertiti did later is one of Egypt’s great debates. Some scholars think she ruled beside Akhenaten as co-regent, or even as king under another name. Others disagree, and the evidence is not conclusive. The face everyone recognizes belongs to a woman nobody can fully place.

mascot.line: When the clues run out, “we don’t know yet” is a perfectly good answer.
